newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks surge to third straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks surge to third straight record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks powered to a record close for the third day in a row Wednesday amid strong buying of blue-chip issues.
"It is amazing, the market rallied on the back of heavyweights Telmex and Televisa, which gave a huge pyschological boost, too," a trader said.
The leading IPC share index closed up 41.84 points, or 1.19 percent, at 3,557.97.

Telecommunications firm Telmex and media group Televisa gained 46 centavos (6 cents) and 5.90 pesos (73 cents), respectively, to 14.78 pesos ($1.89) and 108.30 pesos ($13.84). Their ADRs meanwhile both ended up 1-1/2, at 37-3/4 and 27-3/4 in New York.

"Bullish blue chips are a hallmark of this rally. Televisa in particular has been favoured by an expected operating improvement and lower indebtedness now it has finalised the sale of its stake in Panamsat," said Roberto Galvan, equity analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy firm.
Analysts said the rally also was fuelled by falls in primary interest rates and forecast economic growth.
Several analysts said market fundamentals could sustain the rally for several more sessions.

"The Bolsa looks firm to me. January is always a good month as foreign investors acquire positions for the year. The rally could last at least another three weeks and take us towards a target of 3,600 where it might rest," said Alexander Anderson, an analyst with the Abaco brokerage.
Volume improved over recent sessions to 109.3 million shares traded, which included several hefty cross trades but still reflected interest among foreign investors.
On the broad market, 101 shares changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 49 to 38.
Food company Herdez headed the gainers, up 23 centavos (3 cents) to 2.43 pesos (31 cents).
Beverage firm Emvasa was in second place, up 28 centavos (4 cents) to 4.68 pesos (60 cents), on news it was to sell a $15 million stake in another company.
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek headed the sliders, off 16 centavos (2 cents) to 80 centavos (10 cents), albeit at thin volume.
The most heavily traded loser was financial group GFB, off 1 centavo (1 cent) at 3.12 pesos (40 cents).
